title: Inline Styles
description: Learn when and how to use inline styles in React for dynamic, computed styling.

data.text: React allows you to apply styles directly to elements using the `style` prop. Unlike HTML, React inline styles use camelCase property names and values in an object.

data.title: Inline Style
Dynamic
data.content: Styles based on state or props

data.title: Limitations
data.text: Inline styles don't support pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus), media queries, or CSS animations. Use CSS modules or styled-components for complex styling.

terms.definition: A style object passed directly to an element's style prop.
JavaScript naming convention: backgroundColor instead of background-color.
A style value computed from props, state, or JavaScript expressions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Inline styles use camelCase property names
Values are strings (except for pixel values)
data.takeaway: Use inline styles sparingly - mainly for dynamic values.

data.title: Build a Dynamic Progress Bar
data.description: Create a progress bar component that accepts a percent prop and applies dynamic inline styles.
steps: Use inline styles for width and background color
Change color based on percent thresholds
Add a label showing the percentage
data.expectedOutcome: A progress bar that visually represents progress with dynamic colors.
